source_title: RBI tightens cyber checks on banks amid rising hacks, seeks details on AI risks - India Today
source_excerpt:
The RBI has asked banks to prove cyber compliance and examine API vulnerabilities. The scrutiny follows financial-sector hacks and growing concerns over AI-assisted attacks.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has stepped up scrutiny of banks' cybersecurity preparedness following a spate of cyberattacks on financial institutions, seeking proof of compliance with existing rules and details of their readiness to tackle risks arising from artificial intelligence (AI), reported news agency Reuters.
In a series of recent meetings, the central bank asked banks to examine vulnerabilities in their application programming interfaces (APIs), which are software links that allow banks to connect with non-bank lenders and fintech companies, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters.
The RBI 's increased vigilance comes at a time when banks across the world are facing cyberattacks involving increasingly sophisticated AI tools, putting customer data and funds at risk.
Regulators in countries including the United States and Britain are also stepping up efforts to address AI-related risks, Reuters reported earlier this month.
The RBI has already issued directives to banks on managing cybersecurity risks. However, implementation of these rules has been lagging, a consultant working with top banks told Reuters. This has prompted the central bank to push lenders to ensure stronger implementation of existing requirements.
The central bank's focus on APIs comes amid concerns that weaknesses in the technology connecting banks with other financial institutions could be exploited by hackers.
APIs allow different financial systems to communicate and exchange information. Banks use these connections to work with fintech companies and non-bank lenders, including for services such as loan disbursals.
One of the sources, a person aware of regulatory thinking, told Reuters that hackers view smaller lenders, non-bank lenders and their third-party vendors as "softer targets".
The RBI has therefore asked banks to investigate potential weaknesses in these connections as part of its broader cybersecurity scrutiny.
The RBI's increased vigilance follows a series of cyber incidents involving Indian financial institutions in recent weeks.
At State Bank of India (SBI), the country's largest lender, data belonging to 3,900 customers was leaked . The bank said last week that it was investigating the incident and had yet to determine the vulnerability, according to Reuters.
In another incident, two Mumbai-based non-bank lenders lost around $2 million through more than 700 unauthorised instant transfers from accounts held with ICICI Bank on October 8 and 9.
According to a police complaint reviewed by Reuters, hackers compromised the API link used to send loan disbursal instructions to ICICI Bank.
The incident has brought attention to the risks associated with technology links between banks and non-bank financial institutions, particularly when these are used to facilitate financial transactions.
CERT-IN WARNS OF AI-ASSISTED CYBERATTACKS
India's cybersecurity agency CERT-In had warned in an advisory issued on October 9 that hackers were stealing banks' API credentials to move money out of lenders' own systems, possibly using AI-assisted tools.
Earlier this week, the agency also conducted cybersecurity training for 300 officials from more than 55 financial institutions, CERT-In said in a post on social media platform X.
The RBI's latest push to strengthen cybersecurity checks comes amid growing concerns over the ability of hackers to exploit vulnerabilities in financial infrastructure, including through third-party technology connections and AI-assisted tools.

hi_body:
भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक (आरबीआई) ने वित्तीय संस्थानों की साइबर सुरक्षा तैयारियों की निगरानी को तेज कर दिया है। रिपोर्टों के अनुसार, केंद्रीय बैंक मौजूदा नियमों के अनुपालन के प्रमाण और कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता (एआई) से उत्पन्न होने वाले जोखिमों से निपटने की तैयारियों का विवरण मांग रहा है।

## एपीआई कमजोरियों और एआई जोखिमों पर जोर

समाचार एजेंसियों के अनुसार हालिया बैठकों में केंद्रीय बैंक ने ऋणदाताओं से अपने एप्लिकेशन प्रोग्रामिंग इंटरफेस (एपीआई) की कमजोरियों की जांच करने को कहा है। ये सॉफ्टवेयर लिंक बैंकों को ऋण वितरण सहित विभिन्न सेवाओं के लिए फिनटेक कंपनियों और गैर-बैंकिंग ऋणदाताओं से जुड़ने की अनुमति देते हैं।

रिपोर्ट की गई मुख्य चिंताएं निम्नलिखित हैं:
* हैकर्स द्वारा छोटे ऋणदाताओं और तृतीय-पक्ष विक्रेताओं को आसान निशाना मानना।
* वित्तीय बुनियादी ढांचे को निशाना बनाने वाले एआई-संचालित साइबर हमलों को लेकर बढ़ती वैश्विक चिंता।
* उद्योग सलाहकारों के अनुसार मौजूदा साइबर सुरक्षा निर्देशों के क्रियान्वयन में कमियां।

## हालिया सुरक्षा घटनाएं

यह विनियामक सख्ती हाल के हफ्तों में भारतीय वित्तीय संस्थानों को प्रभावित करने वाली कई साइबर घटनाओं के बाद आई है:
* भारतीय स्टेट बैंक (एसबीआई) ने एक डेटा लीक की जांच करने की बात कही है।
* आईसीआईसीआई बैंक और गैर-बैंकिंग ऋणदाताओं से जुड़ी अनधिकृत लेनदेन की घटनाओं के बाद पुलिस में शिकायतें दर्ज की गई हैं।

## आधिकारिक चेतावनियां और प्रशिक्षण

भारत की साइबर सुरक्षा एजेंसी, सीईआरटी-इन (CERT-In) ने पहले ही चेतावनी जारी की थी कि अनधिकृत तत्व धन निकालने के लिए एपीआई क्रेडेंशियल्स को निशाना बना सकते हैं। इन उभरते खतरों के जवाब में, एजेंसी ने कई वित्तीय संस्थानों के अधिकारियों के लिए प्रशिक्षण सत्र भी आयोजित किए हैं।

## व्यावहारिक निहितार्थ और सत्यापन

वित्तीय संस्थानों से अपेक्षा की जाती है कि वे अपने तृतीय-पक्ष एकीकरण की समीक्षा करें और परिचालन अनुपालन को मजबूत करें। हितधारक भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक और सीईआरटी-इन के आधिकारिक पोर्टलों के माध्यम से विनियामक अपडेट और चेतावनियों का सत्यापन कर सकते हैं।

hi_meta: आरबीआई ने बढ़ते साइबर हमलों और एआई जोखिमों के बीच बैंकों की सुरक्षा जांच कड़ी कर दी है, एपीआई कमजोरियों और अनुपालन पर मांगा विवरण।
en_body:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has increased its scrutiny of the cybersecurity preparedness of financial institutions. According to reports citing sources, the central bank is requesting proof of compliance with existing regulations and details on readiness to manage risks associated with artificial intelligence.

## Focus on API Vulnerabilities and AI Risks

During recent meetings reported by news agencies, the central bank asked lenders to thoroughly examine vulnerabilities within their application programming interfaces (APIs). These software links enable banks to connect with third-party vendors, fintech companies, and non-bank lenders for various operational services, including loan disbursals.

Reported concerns highlight several key areas:
* Hackers allegedly viewing smaller lenders, non-bank financial institutions, and third-party vendors as softer targets.
* Growing international concern over sophisticated, AI-assisted cyberattacks targeting financial infrastructure.
* Gaps in the implementation of existing central bank cybersecurity directives, according to industry consultants.

## Recent Security Incidents

The heightened regulatory attention follows several reported cyber incidents affecting Indian financial entities in recent weeks:
* State Bank of India reported investigating a data leak affecting a limited number of customers.
* Unauthorized transactions involving accounts linked to non-bank lenders and ICICI Bank prompted police complaints regarding compromised API links.

## Official Warnings and Training

India's cybersecurity agency, CERT-In, previously issued advisories warning that unauthorized actors might target API credentials to siphon funds, potentially leveraging AI-driven tools. In response to these evolving threats, CERT-In has also conducted training sessions for officials across multiple financial institutions.

## Practical Implications and Verification

Financial institutions are expected to review their third-party integrations and reinforce operational compliance. Stakeholders and the public can verify official regulatory updates and advisories directly through the official portals of the Reserve Bank of India and CERT-In.
en_title: RBI Tightens Cyber Checks on Banks Amid Rising Hacks, Seeks Details on AI Risks
en_meta: RBI tightens cybersecurity checks on banks, demanding compliance proof and API vulnerability details amid rising AI-assisted threats and financial hacks.
